notes:
POC / evaluation notes:
- Product: building a VS Code copilot (ParseCraft) focused on low-latency inline suggestions + streaming completions.
- Primary ask: streaming token-by-token + robust cancellation so editor doesn't stutter.
- Performance targets: median suggestion delivery <50ms for cached/prefetched completions, p95 < 200ms for typical cold-start sequences.
- Cost sensitivity: want clear token billing for streaming vs non-streaming; evaluate Optimize recommendations to reduce per-token cost during large enterprise usage.
- Model/version pinning: must be able to pin stable model for enterprise customers and route non-critical traffic to cheaper quantized variants.
- Offline/local dev: significant interest in 'local dev mode' (small quantized model running on developer machine) with graceful sync to hosted models for CI.
- Rate limits & auth: need per-org and per-user rate limits for extension marketplace and SSO auth (SAML + optional OIDC). Also wants SDK hooks to expose remaining quota to the extension UI.
- Security: legal asks for SOC2 compliance, KMS integration for key control, audit logs for request/response metadata, retention controls and ability to disable telemetry.
- Quotes from CTO: "We will not sacrifice UX — sub-50ms matters for adoption. Also, no hidden telemetry; customers want opt-out."
- Competitive context: tried OpenAI for early prototyping — saw jitter and retries under burst traffic. Interested in Redwood's routing/fallback capability.
- Engineering notes: implement prefix caching and KV-cache for per-file context to hit latency targets. Evaluate Redwood's batching config to avoid increased tail latency.
- Business: go-to-market plan is extension + enterprise seat licensing; Redwood Dedicated or Private likely for customers in finance/healthcare.
- Risk: Marketplace policy review for extension telemetry could delay launch. Internal SRE wants hard guarantees on cold-start P95.
- Internal stakeholders: CTO (Lina Torres), Eng Lead (Chris Wexler), Product (Ari Gold).
